judgment.notes: M015 is used only in S001 with y=a−1>0 and x=N. The stated a>1 discharges its only source hypothesis; BG001 checks cofinal positive integer thresholds and BG002–BG004 check N(1/N)^a=N^(1−a). Thus this particular limit yields arbitrarily small finite-cover costs at any fixed positive scale. N001 is instantiated at (k,A,s)=(n,E,q), with q>D≥0 from N002, and at (n+1,F,a) or (n+1,F,q+1), with positive exponents. BG001–BG021 record the omitted routine facts with actual source premises and substitutions; their standard real structures and the nontrivial top filter on ℕ meet the native typeclass conditions. No E application occurs. Source fidelity of the direct M015 port is separate from this conditional application review.

S001's N interval pieces have diameter 1/N; M015 and an integer large enough for both scale and cost give H^a_δ(F)=0 for every a>1, and then the dimension bound. S002 correctly obtains q>0 and a cover of cost<ε/2 from N001. Zero-diameter nonempty members are singletons; its displayed positive-radius balls have diameter≤2ρ≤r, positive diameter when n≥1, and q-cost below their dyadic budgets, as checked in BG005–BG013. The original retained cost<ε/2 plus added cost≤ε/2 is strictly<ε; strictness of the whole replacement series is not presumed. S003 uses positive r_i≤1, legitimate ceilings, N_i≤2/r_i, and the Euclidean (rather than maximum) product-distance bound √2 r_i. BG014–BG020 check power signs, constants, countability and finite-subsums control, giving total cost<2(√2)^(q+1)ε. S004 uses 0<min(1,δ/√2)≤1 and √2 r_*≤δ; its finite positive coefficient permits every positive cost threshold, so the content infimum and then the measure supremum are zero. S005 first proves dimension finite and then uses a real midpoint contradiction to reach D+1. Finite or empty index families and interval endpoints cause no exception; no critical-exponent measure assertion or unproved limit exchange is used.
